newsitem.title: GERMANY: EMU timetable must be observed - Germany's Kinkel.
newsitem.headline: EMU timetable must be observed - Germany's Kinkel.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel on Monday insisted that European monetary union must begin as scheduled in 1999 as the opportunity may not present itself again for decades.

In a newspaper article to appear on Tuesday, the 40th anniversary of the signing of the Treaty of Rome which launched today's European Union, Kinkel said it was vital to observe the timetable laid down in the Maastricht Treaty.

"The euro must come on January 1, 1999, as agreed in Maastricht. If we don't grab this chance, it may not come again for decades," Kinkel said in the article, to be published in 25 European newspapers.

Kinkel said it was also essential that the new currency was as stable as possible. "Economic and monetary union is only conceivable as a community of stability," he said in the article, made available in advance by his ministry.
"Germany wants as broad a participation as possible in economic and monetary union -- and from the beginning. No country which durably meets the stability criteria will be excluded," he added.
